runs.content:
Week of 2026-07-30

Dividend Talk
Host: Derek (Ireland) & Edgi (Netherlands)
Why for Fred: Twelve weeks of prior suggestions have been almost entirely US-centric (Invest Like the Best, Acquired, Business Breakdowns, Value Investing with Legends) despite European value investing being the stated core interest. Dividend Talk is run by two European retail-turned-serious investors dissecting names like ASML, Shell, Unilever, and LVMH, with running portfolio-performance reviews and cross-border investing mechanics (currency risk, EU/UK tax treatment) that no US show touches. Closer in register to Pender Fund and Behind the Balance Sheet than to the Colossus network shows already suggested.
Format: Weekly interview/discussion, ~45-60 min
Sample episode: Any recent portfolio-review episode -- search the feed for their latest ASML or LVMH deep dive
Link: https://podcasts.apple.com/podcast/dividend-talk-podcast/id1477731798

Unchained
Host: Laura Shin
Why for Fred: Bankless, Epicenter, Empire, and On The Margin have all been suggested across prior weeks without being picked up -- Unchained is a different register from all four: Shin is an ex-Forbes journalist whose interviews skew toward regulation, institutional custody, security incidents, and the policy fights shaping DeFi/crypto market structure, rather than ecosystem cheerleading or token-economics theory. Recent coverage of stablecoin regulation and institutional custody frameworks maps directly onto the DeFi/Web3 interest from the same investigative angle Fred already favours in Intrigue: To Catch a King.
Format: Long-form interview, 2-3x/week, ~45-60 min
Sample episode: Any recent episode on stablecoin regulation or a major DeFi security incident
Link: https://unchainedcrypto.com/

Dementia Matters
Host: Dr. Nathaniel Chin (University of Wisconsin Alzheimer's Disease Research Center)
Why for Fred: The Peter Attia Drive and Health Longevity Secrets (both previously suggested) cover dementia prevention as one thread within broader longevity content; Dementia Matters is the dedicated clinical-research show, with Chin -- a geriatrician who also cares for his own father through dementia -- interviewing the scientists actually running Alzheimer's prevention trials. Narrower and more clinically specific, matching the dementia-prevention-for-men-~50 focus directly rather than as a subtopic.
Format: Interview, biweekly, ~30-40 min
Sample episode: Any recent episode on modifiable risk factors or a current Alzheimer's prevention trial
Link: https://dementiamatters.wisc.edu/

The Cognitive Revolution
Host: Nathan Labenz & Erik Torenberg
Why for Fred: Dwarkesh, MLST, No Priors, Latent Space, and Me Myself and AI have all been suggested and cover AI from research, science, capital-allocation, engineering, and enterprise-operator angles respectively. Labenz positions himself explicitly as an "AI scout" trying to track everything AI touches as it goes vertical across industries -- closer to a rapid-fire intelligence briefing than a single-lens deep dive, with frequent live-analysis episodes reacting to model releases in near real time. Fills the "staying current on inference trends and AI startups as they happen" gap the slower-cadence shows don't cover.
Format: Interview + live analysis, biweekly (plus rapid-response bonus episodes), ~60-90 min
Sample episode: The most recent live-analysis episode reacting to a frontier model release
Link: https://www.cognitiverevolution.ai/

Week of 2026-07-23

Business Breakdowns
Host: Matt Reustle & Zack Fuss (Colossus)
Why for Fred: The Colossus network sibling to Invest Like the Best and Acquired -- but where Acquired runs 5-8 hour marathons, Business Breakdowns dissects one company per episode in 45-60 minutes: origin, business model, unit economics, competitive moat. The tighter, more frequent format for the same capital-allocation and moat-analysis lens Fred already applies via Berkshire/Buffett principles, without Acquired's multi-week time commitment.
Format: Long-form interview (single-business deep dive), weekly, ~45-60 min
Sample episode: Any recent European or industrial-company breakdown -- check the feed for a name overlapping Fred's portfolio or watchlist sectors
Link: https://www.joincolossus.com/business-breakdowns

Me, Myself, and AI
Host: Sam Ransbotham (MIT Sloan Management Review)
Why for Fred: Fred's AI list so far skews research/capital-allocation (Dwarkesh, No Priors) or engineering (Latent Space, MLST) -- none cover enterprise AI adoption from the inside. Ransbotham interviews executives actually running AI programs at large employers (recent guests include Bank of America on workforce upskilling, Wendy's, Cisco, and OpenAI's in-house economist on labour-market effects). Direct match for the "AI impact on work" thread in Fred's profile, from the operator side.
Format: Long-form interview, biweekly, ~30-40 min
Sample episode: Season 13 finale (June 16, 2026) -- Bank of America on reskilling a global workforce for AI
Link: https://sloanreview.mit.edu/audio-series/me-myself-and-ai/

On The Margin
Host: Michael Ippolito & Tyler Neville (Blockworks)
Why for Fred: Bankless, Epicenter, and Empire (all previously suggested, none picked up) approach DeFi from inside the crypto-native world. On The Margin sits at the seam between macro finance and crypto -- Ippolito interviews traditional asset managers and macro strategists about institutional money treating digital assets as a macro instrument, then closes the week with a co-hosted macro+crypto roundup. Treats the two domains as one conversation instead of two separate hobbies.
Format: Two-part show -- guest interview + roundup, twice weekly, ~45-60 min
Sample episode: "Bitcoin's Role in the Debt End Game" -- Jonah Van Bourg on sovereign debt dynamics and crypto as a macro hedge
Link: https://blockworks.co/podcast/onthemargin

Writing Excuses
Host: Mary Robinette Kowal, Dan Wells, Erin Roberts, DongWon Song, Howard Tayler
Why for Fred: Scriptnotes (suggested last week) covers film/TV screenwriting craft; Writing Excuses is the working-fiction-writer equivalent -- a rotating panel of published novelists and audio-drama veterans (Kowal is also a professional audiobook narrator) dissecting one narrow craft problem per episode. Built to be "fifteen minutes long, because you're in a hurry" -- immediately actionable, mapping more directly onto ongoing production work (Lightfin, The Optimised Jungle) than longer discussion-format shows already on the list.
Format: Panel discussion, weekly, ~15-20 min
Sample episode: Any episode tagged "structure" or "worldbuilding" -- check the archive for one matching a current Lightfin story problem
Link: https://writingexcuses.com/
